citation.title: Research on topology optimization of carbon fiber reinforced composite electric vehicle helmet based on deep learning
citation.authors: Xiangkui Zhang, Wei Wei, Ping Hu, Chengxiang Han
citation.venue: Journal of Physics: Conference Series, published 1 July 2024
citation.version_coded: No version of the full text was accessible. Coded from the abstract obtained via the public Crossref API (api.crossref.org/works/10.1088/1742-6596/2791/1/012064), identical to the abstract already stored in audit/pool/pool.csv for this pid.

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The abstract describes a U-Net trained on data generated by a variable-density (SIMP-type) method to predict a 2D topology-optimized pattern for a dimensionality-reduced (3D-to-2D unrolled) carbon-fiber helmet shell, then maps the result back to 3D; the optimized helmet is reported to have stronger stiffness and energy-absorption performance than an ordinary helmet of the same mass. No computational speed or cost comparison with a classical method is stated in the abstract.
claim.key_phrase: stiffness performance and energy absorption effect of the optimized helmet are stronger
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not applicable: the abstract makes no speed, runtime or computational-cost claim of any kind; the only comparison stated is a downstream design-quality one (stiffness and energy absorption of the optimized vs. ordinary helmet at equal mass), with no numeric values given in the abstract itself.
claim.alternatives: None identifiable from the abstract alone; full text is inaccessible.

baseline.classical_method: Variable density method (referred to in the abstract as the 'Isotropic Material Penalty Density method', i.e. SIMP), used to generate the training dataset for the U-Net, and implicitly represented by the 'ordinary helmet' used as the comparison baseline in simulation
baseline.problem_size: not stated (abstract only); a 3D helmet shell model, unrolled to 2D grids via a 'one-step inverse forming method'
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated (abstract only); training data are generated by running the variable-density method, per the abstract, but no cost figure is given
baseline.quality_metric: Stiffness and energy-absorption performance from simulation of the optimized vs. ordinary helmet 'under the same quality' (mass), per the abstract; no specific metric values or FE-verification detail given
baseline.quality_gap: not stated numerically in the abstract

reporting.n_test_cases: not stated in the abstract; appears to be a single helmet design comparison ('the ordinary helmet and the optimized helmet')
